---- MODULE W4Od11m8p0t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Jobs, Printers, NoJob

MaxCap == 2

VARIABLES coarse, fine, phase, assign, capacity
vars == << coarse, fine, phase, assign, capacity >>

Printing == { j \in Jobs : phase[j] = "printing" }

TypeOK ==
  /\ coarse \in Jobs \cup {NoJob}
  /\ fine \in [Printers -> Jobs \cup {NoJob}]
  /\ phase \in [Jobs -> {"idle", "coarse", "fine", "printing", "done"}]
  /\ assign \in [Jobs -> Printers]
  /\ capacity \in 1..MaxCap

Init ==
  /\ coarse = NoJob
  /\ fine = [p \in Printers |-> NoJob]
  /\ phase = [j \in Jobs |-> "idle"]
  /\ assign \in [Jobs -> Printers]
  /\ capacity = MaxCap

TakeCoarse(j) ==
  /\ phase[j] = "idle"
  /\ coarse = NoJob
  /\ coarse' = j
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![j] = "coarse"]
  /\ UNCHANGED << fine, assign, capacity >>

TakeFine(j) ==
  /\ phase[j] = "coarse"
  /\ coarse = j
  /\ fine[assign[j]] = NoJob
  /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![assign[j]] = j]
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![j] = "fine"]
  /\ coarse' = NoJob
  /\ UNCHANGED << assign, capacity >>

StartPrint(j) ==
  /\ phase[j] = "fine"
  /\ Cardinality(Printing) < capacity
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![j] = "printing"]
  /\ UNCHANGED << coarse, fine, assign, capacity >>

FinishPrint(j) ==
  /\ phase[j] = "printing"
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![j] = "done"]
  /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![assign[j]] = NoJob]
  /\ UNCHANGED << coarse, assign, capacity >>

Retune(c) ==
  /\ c \in 1..MaxCap
  /\ c # capacity
  /\ capacity' = c
  /\ UNCHANGED << coarse, fine, phase, assign >>

Next ==
  \/ \E j \in Jobs : TakeCoarse(j) \/ TakeFine(j) \/ StartPrint(j) \/ FinishPrint(j)
  \/ \E c \in 1..MaxCap : Retune(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

HierarchyOK ==
  /\ \A j1, j2 \in Jobs :
       (phase[j1] = "printing" /\ phase[j2] = "printing" /\ assign[j1] = assign[j2])
         => j1 = j2
  /\ \A j \in Jobs : phase[j] = "printing" => fine[assign[j]] = j
  /\ \A j \in Jobs : phase[j] = "coarse" => coarse = j
  /\ Cardinality(Printing) <= MaxCap
====
nl:
A print shop runs a job spooler in front of two physical printers. Every submitted job
must climb a two-level lock hierarchy before it can put ink on paper: first it takes the
single shop-wide coarse lock, and only while holding that coarse lock may it reserve the
fine per-printer lock for the specific printer it has been assigned. Once a job owns the
fine lock for its printer it releases the coarse lock and begins printing, so other jobs
can start climbing the hierarchy on a different printer meanwhile. When a job finishes it
drops the fine lock for its printer and leaves the system.

The shop floor is not static: a supervisor can raise or lower the concurrent-printing
capacity at runtime, for instance when one printer is pulled aside for a toner change.
Lowering the capacity never evicts jobs that are already printing; it only prevents new
jobs from starting until enough jobs have drained.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A printer is never printing two different jobs at once, a job only ever
prints while it holds that printer's fine lock, only the holder of the coarse lock is in
the middle of acquiring a fine lock, and the number of jobs printing never exceeds the
capacity in force when they started.

---- MODULE W4Od2m9p5t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Robots, NoBot
MaxEpoch == 3

VARIABLES epoch, robotEpoch, crashed, sealed, sealer, sealEpoch
vars == << epoch, robotEpoch, crashed, sealed, sealer, sealEpoch >>

TypeOK ==
  /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
  /\ robotEpoch \in [Robots -> 0..MaxEpoch]
  /\ crashed \in [Robots -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ sealed \in BOOLEAN
  /\ sealer \in Robots \cup {NoBot}
  /\ sealEpoch \in 0..MaxEpoch

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ robotEpoch = [r \in Robots |-> 0]
  /\ crashed = [r \in Robots |-> FALSE]
  /\ sealed = FALSE
  /\ sealer = NoBot
  /\ sealEpoch = 0

Republish ==
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED << robotEpoch, crashed, sealed, sealer, sealEpoch >>

Adopt(r) ==
  /\ ~crashed[r]
  /\ robotEpoch[r] < epoch
  /\ robotEpoch' = [robotEpoch EXCEPT ![r] = epoch]
  /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, crashed, sealed, sealer, sealEpoch >>

CrashSilently(r) ==
  /\ ~crashed[r]
  /\ crashed' = [crashed EXCEPT ![r] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, robotEpoch, sealed, sealer, sealEpoch >>

Repair(r) ==
  /\ crashed[r]
  /\ crashed' = [crashed EXCEPT ![r] = FALSE]
  /\ robotEpoch' = [robotEpoch EXCEPT ![r] = 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, sealed, sealer, sealEpoch >>

SealTrailer(r) ==
  /\ ~sealed
  /\ ~crashed[r]
  /\ robotEpoch[r] = epoch
  /\ sealed' = TRUE
  /\ sealer' = r
  /\ sealEpoch' = robotEpoch[r]
  /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, robotEpoch, crashed >>

Next ==
  \/ Republish
  \/ \E r \in Robots : Adopt(r) \/ CrashSilently(r) \/ Repair(r) \/ SealTrailer(r)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

SealOnceOK ==
  /\ (sealed = (sealer \in Robots))
  /\ (sealed => sealEpoch <= epoch)
  /\ (~sealed => sealEpoch = 0)
  /\ \A r \in Robots : robotEpoch[r] <= epoch
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Robots = {r1, r2, r3}
  NoBot = NoBot
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT SealOnceOK
nl:
A warehouse runs a fleet of picking robots under a coordinator that publishes numbered
configurations. Every time the floor plan changes the coordinator increments the epoch
number; each robot picks up the new epoch on its own schedule, so at any moment some
robots are still operating on a stale epoch. Exactly one irreversible act exists in this
system: sealing the outbound trailer. A robot may seal the trailer only if it is running
on the current epoch and has not crashed, and once the trailer is sealed nobody can seal
it again or unseal it. The system records which robot sealed it and under which epoch.

Robots can crash silently: a crashed robot stops adopting epochs and stops working, and
nothing in the system is notified. A crashed robot never seals the trailer. A technician can power-cycle a crashed robot at
any time; it comes back alive but with its epoch memory wiped back to zero, so it must
re-adopt the published epoch before it can do anything consequential.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The trailer is sealed at most once, a sealer is always recorded exactly
when the trailer is sealed, the recorded seal epoch never runs ahead of the published epoch, an unsealed
trailer carries no recorded seal epoch, and no robot ever runs an epoch ahead of the coordinator's published epoch.

---- MODULE W4Od4m9p2t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Bays
Total == 6
BayCap == 2
MaxEpoch == 2

VARIABLES reservoir, loaded, sump, epoch, bayEpoch, override
vars == << reservoir, loaded, sump, epoch, bayEpoch, override >>

RECURSIVE SumOver(_)
SumOver(S) ==
  IF S = {} THEN 0
  ELSE LET b == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN loaded[b] + SumOver(S \ {b})

InBays == SumOver(Bays)

TypeOK ==
  /\ reservoir \in 0..Total
  /\ sump \in 0..Total
  /\ loaded \in [Bays -> 0..BayCap]
  /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
  /\ bayEpoch \in [Bays -> 0..MaxEpoch]
  /\ override \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
  /\ reservoir = Total
  /\ sump = 0
  /\ loaded = [b \in Bays |-> 0]
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ bayEpoch = [b \in Bays |-> 0]
  /\ override = FALSE

MayDraw(b) == override \/ bayEpoch[b] = epoch

Draw(b) ==
  /\ MayDraw(b)
  /\ reservoir > 0
  /\ loaded[b] < BayCap
  /\ reservoir' = reservoir - 1
  /\ loaded' = [loaded EXCEPT ![b] = loaded[b] + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED << sump, epoch, bayEpoch, override >>

Discharge(b) ==
  /\ loaded[b] > 0
  /\ loaded' = [loaded EXCEPT ![b] = loaded[b] - 1]
  /\ sump' = sump + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED << reservoir, epoch, bayEpoch, override >>

Filter ==
  /\ sump > 0
  /\ sump' = sump - 1
  /\ reservoir' = reservoir + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED << loaded, epoch, bayEpoch, override >>

Retune ==
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED << reservoir, loaded, sump, bayEpoch, override >>

CatchUp(b) ==
  /\ bayEpoch[b] < epoch
  /\ bayEpoch' = [bayEpoch EXCEPT ![b] = epoch]
  /\ UNCHANGED << reservoir, loaded, sump, epoch, override >>

ToggleOverride ==
  /\ override' = ~override
  /\ UNCHANGED << reservoir, loaded, sump, epoch, bayEpoch >>

Next ==
  \/ \E b \in Bays : Draw(b) \/ Discharge(b) \/ CatchUp(b)
  \/ Filter \/ Retune \/ ToggleOverride

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

WaterConserved ==
  /\ reservoir + InBays + sump = Total
  /\ \A b \in Bays : loaded[b] <= BayCap
  /\ reservoir >= 0 /\ sump >= 0
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Bays = {north, south}
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT WaterConserved
nl:
An automatic car wash recirculates its water. The plant holds a fixed total volume of
water that is always somewhere: in the clean reservoir, loaded inside one of the wash
bays, or sitting in the reclaim sump waiting to be filtered back. A bay draws water from
the reservoir when a car enters, returns most of it to the sump when the car leaves, and
the filtration unit moves water from the sump back to the reservoir.

The conveyor's speed and chemistry are governed by numbered configurations. Whenever the
plant is retuned the configuration epoch is incremented, and a bay may only draw water
while it is running the currently published epoch, so a stale bay stalls until it catches
up. Retuning never adds or removes water.

A plant supervisor holds an override key. With the override engaged, a bay may draw water
without being on the current epoch, which is how a car already mid-tunnel gets rinsed
after an emergency retune. The override changes who may act, never how much water exists.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The water in the reservoir, the water loaded in the bays, and the water
in the reclaim sump always sum to exactly the plant's fixed total, no bay ever holds more
than its capacity, and no compartment ever goes negative.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od15m5p5t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Members, Prices
Quorum == 3

VARIABLES cast, inflight, counted, printed, openPrice, witness
vars == << cast, inflight, counted, printed, openPrice, witness >>

Approvals == { m \in counted : cast[m] = "approve" }
Rejections == { m \in counted : cast[m] = "reject" }

TypeOK ==
  /\ cast \in [Members -> {"none", "approve", "reject"}]
  /\ inflight \subseteq Members
  /\ counted \subseteq Members
  /\ printed \in BOOLEAN
  /\ openPrice \in Prices \cup {0}
  /\ witness \subseteq Members

Init ==
  /\ cast = [m \in Members |-> "none"]
  /\ inflight = {}
  /\ counted = {}
  /\ printed = FALSE
  /\ openPrice = 0
  /\ witness = {}

CastBallot(m, v) ==
  /\ cast[m] = "none"
  /\ v \in {"approve", "reject"}
  /\ cast' = [cast EXCEPT ![m] = v]
  /\ inflight' = inflight \cup {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED << counted, printed, openPrice, witness >>

DeliverBallot(m) ==
  /\ m \in inflight
  /\ inflight' = inflight \ {m}
  /\ counted' = counted \cup {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED << cast, printed, openPrice, witness >>

PrintOpen(p) ==
  /\ ~printed
  /\ p \in Prices
  /\ Cardinality(Approvals) >= Quorum
  /\ printed' = TRUE
  /\ openPrice' = p
  /\ witness' = Approvals
  /\ UNCHANGED << cast, inflight, counted >>

Abstain(m) ==
  /\ cast[m] = "none"
  /\ m \notin inflight
  /\ cast' = [cast EXCEPT ![m] = "reject"]
  /\ counted' = counted \cup {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED << inflight, printed, openPrice, witness >>

RedeliverBallot(m) ==
  /\ m \in counted
  /\ counted' = counted \cup {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED << cast, inflight, printed, openPrice, witness >>

EngineIdle == UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
  \/ EngineIdle
  \/ \E m \in Members : \E v \in {"approve", "reject"} : CastBallot(m, v)
  \/ \E m \in Members : DeliverBallot(m) \/ Abstain(m) \/ RedeliverBallot(m)
  \/ \E p \in Prices : PrintOpen(p)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

AuctionOK ==
  /\ (printed = (openPrice \in Prices))
  /\ (printed => /\ witness \subseteq counted
                 /\ Cardinality(witness) >= Quorum
                 /\ \A m \in witness : cast[m] = "approve")
  /\ (~printed => witness = {})
  /\ counted \cap inflight = {}
  /\ \A m \in counted \cup inflight : cast[m] # "none"
  /\ ~(Cardinality(Approvals) >= Quorum /\ Cardinality(Rejections) >= Quorum)
====
nl:
Before a stock exchange opens for continuous trading it runs an opening auction. The
member firms on the opening committee each cast a ballot approving or rejecting the
indicative opening price. Ballots travel over the exchange's message bus, which makes no
ordering guarantee: a ballot cast later can be delivered first, and a ballot sits in
flight for an arbitrary time before the tally counts it.

The auction closes with one irreversible act: printing the opening price. The engine may
print only once it has counted approving ballots from a quorum of the committee, and once
the opening print has been published it can never be republished, revised, or withdrawn.
Ballots that are still in flight when the print happens are still delivered and counted,
but they cannot cause a second print. When the engine prints, it files the exact set of approving
ballots that justified the print as the auction's witness record. The engine may also simply idle, leaving the auction state untouched. The bus also delivers at least once rather than
exactly once, so an already-counted ballot may be handed to the tally again; a redelivery
must leave the tally exactly as it was.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A price is recorded exactly when the auction has printed, the filed witness record is always a set of counted approving ballots of at
least quorum size when printed and empty when unprinted, no ballot is
counted while still in flight or counted before it was cast, and the committee can never
simultaneously show a quorum for approval and a quorum for rejection.

---- MODULE W4Od18m9p4t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Locks
HardLimit == 2
MaxEpoch == 2

VARIABLES hubEpoch, lockEpoch, open, allowance, override
vars == << hubEpoch, lockEpoch, open, allowance, override >>

TypeOK ==
  /\ hubEpoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
  /\ lockEpoch \in [Locks -> 0..MaxEpoch]
  /\ open \subseteq Locks
  /\ allowance \in 0..HardLimit
  /\ override \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
  /\ hubEpoch = 0
  /\ lockEpoch = [l \in Locks |-> 0]
  /\ open = {}
  /\ allowance = HardLimit
  /\ override = FALSE

Current(e) == { l \in Locks : lockEpoch[l] = e }

Republish ==
  /\ hubEpoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ hubEpoch' = hubEpoch + 1
  /\ open' = IF override THEN open ELSE open \cap Current(hubEpoch + 1)
  /\ UNCHANGED << lockEpoch, allowance, override >>

Sync(l) ==
  /\ lockEpoch[l] < hubEpoch
  /\ lockEpoch' = [lockEpoch EXCEPT ![l] = hubEpoch]
  /\ UNCHANGED << hubEpoch, open, allowance, override >>

Unlock(l) ==
  /\ l \notin open
  /\ (lockEpoch[l] = hubEpoch \/ override)
  /\ Cardinality(open) + 1 <= allowance
  /\ open' = open \cup {l}
  /\ UNCHANGED << hubEpoch, lockEpoch, allowance, override >>

Relock(l) ==
  /\ l \in open
  /\ open' = open \ {l}
  /\ UNCHANGED << hubEpoch, lockEpoch, allowance, override >>

SetAllowance(k) ==
  /\ k \in 0..HardLimit
  /\ k # allowance
  /\ k >= Cardinality(open)
  /\ allowance' = k
  /\ UNCHANGED << hubEpoch, lockEpoch, open, override >>

ToggleOverride ==
  /\ override' = ~override
  /\ open' = IF override THEN open \cap Current(hubEpoch) ELSE open
  /\ UNCHANGED << hubEpoch, lockEpoch, allowance >>

Next ==
  \/ \E l \in Locks : Sync(l) \/ Unlock(l) \/ Relock(l)
  \/ \E k \in 0..HardLimit : SetAllowance(k)
  \/ Republish \/ ToggleOverride

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

OccupancyOK ==
  /\ Cardinality(open) <= allowance
  /\ allowance <= HardLimit
  /\ \A l \in Locks : lockEpoch[l] <= hubEpoch
  /\ \A l \in open : (lockEpoch[l] = hubEpoch \/ override)
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Locks = {front, back, garage}
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT OccupancyOK
nl:
A smart-home network controls the door locks of a house from a hub. The hub publishes a
numbered security configuration; each lock caches the epoch number it last synced, and a
lock that has not synced the current epoch is considered stale. Under normal operation a
lock may only be opened while it is running the hub's current epoch, which is how a
revoked key stops working the moment the homeowner republishes the configuration.

The hub enforces an occupancy rule: at most a fixed number of doors may stand unlocked at
the same time, so the house is never wide open. The homeowner can lower or raise that
allowance, but never above the hardware limit burned into the hub.

An installer override exists for service visits. While the override is engaged a stale
lock may still be opened, because the technician's tool talks to the lock directly. The
override relaxes who may open a door; it never relaxes how many doors may be open.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of unlocked doors never exceeds the currently allowed
occupancy, the allowance itself never exceeds the hub's hardware limit, no lock ever
caches an epoch newer than the hub's, and a stale lock is only ever unlocked while the
installer override is engaged.

---- MODULE W4Od1m7p3t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Slots, Flights, Instances, Free

VARIABLES reg, scratch, target, held
vars == << reg, scratch, target, held >>

TypeOK ==
  /\ reg \in [Slots -> Flights \cup {Free}]
  /\ scratch \in [Instances -> [Slots -> Flights \cup {Free}]]
  /\ target \in [Instances -> Flights \cup {Free}]
  /\ held \in [Flights -> Slots \cup {Free}]

Init ==
  /\ reg = [s \in Slots |-> Free]
  /\ scratch = [i \in Instances |-> [s \in Slots |-> Free]]
  /\ target = [i \in Instances |-> Free]
  /\ held = [f \in Flights |-> Free]

PickFlight(i, f) ==
  /\ target[i] = Free
  /\ held[f] = Free
  /\ \A j \in Instances : target[j] # f
  /\ target' = [target EXCEPT ![i] = f]
  /\ UNCHANGED << reg, scratch, held >>

ReadSlot(i, s) ==
  /\ target[i] # Free
  /\ scratch' = [scratch EXCEPT ![i][s] = reg[s]]
  /\ UNCHANGED << reg, target, held >>

SwapClaim(i, s) ==
  /\ target[i] # Free
  /\ scratch[i][s] = Free
  /\ reg[s] = Free
  /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![s] = target[i]]
  /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![target[i]] = s]
  /\ target' = [target EXCEPT ![i] = Free]
  /\ scratch' = [scratch EXCEPT ![i][s] = target[i]]

SwapFails(i, s) ==
  /\ target[i] # Free
  /\ scratch[i][s] # reg[s]
  /\ scratch' = [scratch EXCEPT ![i][s] = reg[s]]
  /\ UNCHANGED << reg, target, held >>

ReleaseSlot(i, f) ==
  /\ held[f] \in Slots
  /\ reg[held[f]] = f
  /\ scratch[i][held[f]] = f
  /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![held[f]] = Free]
  /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![f] = Free]
  /\ scratch' = [scratch EXCEPT ![i][held[f]] = Free]
  /\ UNCHANGED << target >>

Next ==
  \/ \E i \in Instances, f \in Flights : PickFlight(i, f) \/ ReleaseSlot(i, f)
  \/ \E i \in Instances, s \in Slots : ReadSlot(i, s) \/ SwapClaim(i, s) \/ SwapFails(i, s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

AllocationOK ==
  /\ \A s1, s2 \in Slots :
       (reg[s1] # Free /\ reg[s1] = reg[s2]) => s1 = s2
  /\ \A f \in Flights : (held[f] \in Slots) => reg[held[f]] = f
  /\ \A s \in Slots : (reg[s] \in Flights) => held[reg[s]] = s
  /\ \A i \in Instances : target[i] \in Flights => held[target[i]] = Free
====
nl:
An airport runs two independent runway-allocator instances, a primary in the tower and a
backup in the approach centre. Both write to the same shared slot register: a table that
maps each landing slot either to the flight that owns it or to a free marker. Neither
instance trusts the other, so both use compare-and-swap. An instance first reads the
current contents of a slot into its local scratch, then attempts a swap that succeeds only
if the register still holds exactly what it read; otherwise the swap fails and the
instance must re-read before trying again.

Both instances draw flights from one shared pool of arriving aircraft, so the same flight
can be worked on by either instance, and a flight already holding a slot is never given a
second one. A flight that lands releases its slot back to free by the same read-then-swap
discipline.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No landing slot is ever recorded as owned by two different flights and no
flight ever holds two slots at once, the register and the allocators' bookkeeping always
agree about who owns what, and a swap never takes effect on a slot whose contents changed
since the reading instance last looked.

---- MODULE W4Od12m1p0t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Terminals, Nobody

VARIABLES holder, transit, inside, units, sent
vars == << holder, transit, inside, units, sent >>

MaxUnits == 3

TypeOK ==
  /\ holder \in Terminals \cup {Nobody}
  /\ transit \subseteq Terminals
  /\ inside \subseteq Terminals
  /\ units \in 0..MaxUnits
  /\ sent \in 0..MaxUnits

Init ==
  /\ holder \in Terminals
  /\ transit = {}
  /\ inside = {}
  /\ units = MaxUnits
  /\ sent = 0

EnterRoutine(t) ==
  /\ holder = t
  /\ t \notin inside
  /\ inside' = inside \cup {t}
  /\ UNCHANGED << holder, transit, units, sent >>

AdjustUnits(t) ==
  /\ t \in inside
  /\ units > 0
  /\ units' = units - 1
  /\ sent' = sent + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED << holder, transit, inside >>

LeaveRoutine(t) ==
  /\ t \in inside
  /\ inside' = inside \ {t}
  /\ UNCHANGED << holder, transit, units, sent >>

Forward(t, u) ==
  /\ holder = t
  /\ inside = {}
  /\ u # t
  /\ holder' = Nobody
  /\ transit' = {u}
  /\ UNCHANGED << inside, units, sent >>

Deliver(u) ==
  /\ u \in transit
  /\ holder = Nobody
  /\ holder' = u
  /\ transit' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED << inside, units, sent >>

Next ==
  \/ \E t \in Terminals : EnterRoutine(t) \/ AdjustUnits(t) \/ LeaveRoutine(t)
  \/ \E t, u \in Terminals : Forward(t, u)
  \/ \E u \in Terminals : Deliver(u)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

TokenOK ==
  /\ \A t1, t2 \in inside : t1 = t2
  /\ \A t \in inside : holder = t
  /\ ((holder \in Terminals) => transit = {})
  /\ ((holder = Nobody) => \E u \in Terminals : transit = {u})
  /\ units + sent = MaxUnits
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Terminals = {north, south, west}
  Nobody = Nobody
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT TokenOK
nl:
A regional blood bank tracks its inventory from several branch terminals. Only one
terminal at a time may enter the reconciliation routine that adjusts unit counts, and the
right to enter is carried by a single circulating token. A terminal that finishes
reconciling hands the token onward as a message addressed to another terminal.

The branch network delivers token messages without ordering guarantees: a handoff sent
earlier may arrive after one sent later, and a token may sit in transit for a long time.
While a token is in transit no terminal holds it, so nobody may reconcile. A terminal
accepts a token addressed to it, becomes the holder, may enter and later leave the
reconciliation routine, and eventually forwards the token again.

SAFETY PROPERTY: At most one terminal is ever inside the reconciliation routine and only a
token holder can be inside it; the token itself is never duplicated or lost, so at every
moment it is either held by exactly one terminal or in transit to exactly one terminal,
never both and never neither.

---- MODULE W4Od18m4p0t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Controllers, Commands, Idle
Depth == 2

VARIABLES queue, actuator, outstanding, applied, refused
vars == << queue, actuator, outstanding, applied, refused >>

Queued == { queue[i] : i \in 1..Len(queue) }

TypeOK ==
  /\ queue \in Seq(Commands)
  /\ actuator \in Commands \cup {Idle}
  /\ outstanding \in [Controllers -> Commands \cup {Idle}]
  /\ applied \subseteq Commands
  /\ refused \in 0..Depth

Init ==
  /\ queue = << >>
  /\ actuator = Idle
  /\ outstanding = [c \in Controllers |-> Idle]
  /\ applied = {}
  /\ refused = 0

Submit(c, k) ==
  /\ outstanding[c] = Idle
  /\ k \notin Queued
  /\ k # actuator
  /\ \A d \in Controllers : outstanding[d] # k
  /\ Len(queue) < Depth
  /\ queue' = Append(queue, k)
  /\ outstanding' = [outstanding EXCEPT ![c] = k]
  /\ UNCHANGED << actuator, applied, refused >>

Refuse(c, k) ==
  /\ outstanding[c] = Idle
  /\ Len(queue) = Depth
  /\ k \in Commands
  /\ refused < Depth
  /\ refused' = refused + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED << queue, actuator, outstanding, applied >>

  /\ Len(queue) > 0
  /\ actuator = Idle
  /\ actuator' = Head(queue)
  /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
  /\ UNCHANGED << outstanding, applied, refused >>

  /\ actuator # Idle
  /\ applied' = applied \cup {actuator}
  /\ outstanding' = [c \in Controllers |->
       IF outstanding[c] = actuator THEN Idle ELSE outstanding[c]]
  /\ actuator' = Idle
  /\ UNCHANGED << queue, refused >>

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in Controllers, k \in Commands : Submit(c, k) \/ Refuse(c, k)
  \/ Dispatch \/ Complete

  /\ Len(queue) <= Depth
  /\ actuator \notin Queued
  /\ \A i, j \in 1..Len(queue) : queue[i] = queue[j] => i = j

nl:
A house runs two independent smart-lock controllers, the wall panel and the phone app.
Both draw from one shared pool of door commands and both feed the same bounded command
queue in the lock bridge. The queue has a fixed depth; when it is full a controller's
submission is refused outright and the controller must back off rather than block, which
is the bridge's backpressure rule.

The bridge has a single radio actuator, and that actuator is the critical resource: it can
be driving exactly one command at a time. The bridge takes the command at the head of the
queue, occupies the actuator for the duration of the radio exchange, and only then frees
the actuator and records the command as applied. A command is never in the queue and on
the actuator simultaneously, and a controller has at most one command outstanding. A command that has already been
applied may be issued again later -- doors get locked and unlocked repeatedly -- but never
while a copy of it is still queued, on the actuator, or outstanding at either controller.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The actuator drives at most one command at a time and only a command that
was accepted into the queue, the queue never grows past its fixed depth, no command is
both queued and on the actuator, and no controller has more than one command outstanding.

nl:
An airport baggage router accepts scan events from handheld scanners at the check-in
desks and feeds them into a bounded routing queue. Each scanner carries a credential
stamped with the security epoch it was issued under. Operations rotates the epoch during
a shift -- after a crew change, for instance -- and a scanner whose credential predates
the current epoch is stale: the router refuses its scans until the scanner re-credentials
at a desk terminal.

The routing queue applies backpressure. Its depth is not fixed: the duty manager can raise
it when a bank of flights checks in and lower it again afterwards, but lowering it never
discards work already queued -- the queue simply refuses new scans until it drains below
the new depth. A refused scan is counted so the desk can see the pushback.

Every accepted scan records the scanner that produced it and the epoch that scanner held
when the scan was accepted, so the router can always audit that only current credentials
put work into the system.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every scan sitting in the routing queue was accepted from a real scanner
holding the epoch recorded on that scan, no queued scan carries an epoch newer than the
current security epoch, no scanner's credential is ever newer than the current epoch, the
queue never holds more scans than the router's hard maximum, and because the queue is FIFO
and the epoch only ever moves forward, the recorded epochs never decrease along the queue.

vars == << clock, owner, deadline, holds, override >>

  /\ owner \in [Slots -> Flights \cup {Unowned}]
  /\ deadline \in [Slots -> 0..(Horizon + LeaseLen)]
  /\ holds \in [Flights -> Slots \cup {Unowned}]
  /\ override \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
  /\ clock = 0
  /\ owner = [s \in Slots |-> Unowned]
  /\ deadline = [s \in Slots |-> 0]
  /\ holds = [f \in Flights |-> Unowned]
  /\ override = FALSE

GrantLease(s, f) ==
  /\ owner[s] = Unowned
  /\ holds[f] = Unowned
  /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![s] = f]
  /\ deadline' = [deadline EXCEPT ![s] = clock + LeaseLen]
  /\ holds' = [holds EXCEPT ![f] = s]
  /\ UNCHANGED << clock, override >>

RenewLease(s) ==
  /\ owner[s] # Unowned
  /\ deadline[s] > clock
  /\ deadline' = [deadline EXCEPT ![s] = clock + LeaseLen]
  /\ UNCHANGED << clock, owner, holds, override >>

Expire(s) ==
  /\ owner[s] # Unowned
  /\ deadline[s] <= clock
  /\ holds' = [holds EXCEPT ![owner[s]] = Unowned]
  /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![s] = Unowned]
  /\ deadline' = [deadline EXCEPT ![s] = 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED << clock, override >>

TickClock ==
  /\ clock < Horizon
  /\ clock' = clock + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED << owner, deadline, holds, override >>

ArmOverride ==
  /\ override' = ~override
  /\ UNCHANGED << clock, owner, deadline, holds >>

Revoke(s) ==
  /\ override
  /\ owner[s] # Unowned
  /\ holds' = [holds EXCEPT ![owner[s]] = Unowned]
  /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![s] = Unowned]
  /\ deadline' = [deadline EXCEPT ![s] = 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED << clock, override >>

Next ==
  \/ \E s \in Slots, f \in Flights : GrantLease(s, f)
  \/ \E s \in Slots : RenewLease(s) \/ Expire(s) \/ Revoke(s)
  \/ TickClock \/ ArmOverride

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

LeaseOK ==
  /\ \A s1, s2 \in Slots :
       (owner[s1] # Unowned /\ owner[s1] = owner[s2]) => s1 = s2
  /\ \A f \in Flights : holds[f] \in Slots => owner[holds[f]] = f
  /\ \A s \in Slots : owner[s] \in Flights => holds[owner[s]] = s
  /\ \A s \in Slots : owner[s] = Unowned => deadline[s] = 0
====
nl:
A runway allocator hands out landing slots as timed leases rather than permanent grants.
When a flight is given a slot the allocator stamps the lease with a deadline drawn from
the tower clock. The flight must renew before the deadline; the moment the clock passes a
lease's deadline the lease is dead and the allocator reclaims the slot for someone else.
A reclaimed slot carries no owner and no deadline.

The supervisor at the tower has an override. With the override armed the supervisor can
revoke a live lease outright -- to clear a slot for a medical emergency, say -- and can
grant a slot to a flight without waiting for the ordinary sequencing. The override never
lets two flights hold the same slot and never resurrects an expired lease: a revoked slot
goes back to unowned first, and only then can it be granted again.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A slot is never leased to two flights and a flight never holds two slots
at once, an unowned slot carries no deadline at all, and the allocator's flight-to-slot record always agrees with the
lease table in both directions.

  /\ version[s] < MaxVer
  /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![s] = Nil]
  /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![s] = version[s] + 1]

  \/ \E d \in Desks, f \in Flights : TakeFlight(d, f)
  \/ \E d \in Desks, s \in Slots : ReadSlot(d, s) \/ CommitWrite(d, s) \/ RejectWrite(d, s)

Two runway allocator instances -- the tower desk and the flow-control desk -- share one
pool of arriving flights and one slot table, and neither takes a lock. The slot table
carries a version stamp per slot. An instance that wants a slot for a flight first reads
the slot's owner and version into its own workspace, then tries to write the assignment
back. The write is accepted only if the slot's version is still the one it read; if
another instance got there first the version has moved on, the write is rejected, and the
instance records a retry and must read again. Every accepted write bumps the version.

Both desks pull from the same flight pool, so the same flight can be picked up by either
desk, and a flight that already has a slot is never picked up again.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No slot is ever assigned to two flights and no flight ever holds two
slots, a flight being worked on by a desk does not already own a slot, a slot that has
never been written still carries version zero, and no instance's cached version is ever
ahead of the slot's real version.

Two runway allocator desks share one pool of flights, and every slot assignment is agreed

opens a transaction by proposing that a named flight take a named slot. Only one
transaction may be open at a time. Radar and ground each vote yes or no on the open
proposal. If both vote yes the desk commits, and only then is the slot written into the
assignment table. If either votes no the desk aborts and nothing is written. Either way
the proposal is cleared and the votes are reset before another transaction can open.

Because both desks work the same flight pool, a proposal is only allowed for a flight that
holds no slot yet and for a slot that is currently unassigned.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The assignment table never gives one slot to two flights or one flight
two slots, an assignment only ever appears as the result of a transaction that both radar
and ground voted yes on, and while no transaction is open there are no outstanding votes.

  /\ leader \in Cranes \cup {NoLeader}
  /\ craneTerm \in [Cranes -> 0..MaxTerm]
  /\ manifest \subseteq Moves
  /\ acked \subseteq Moves

  /\ term = 0
  /\ leader = NoLeader
  /\ craneTerm = [c \in Cranes |-> 0]

StandForElection(c) ==
  /\ term < MaxTerm
  /\ term' = term + 1
  /\ leader' = c
  /\ craneTerm' = [craneTerm EXCEPT ![c] = term + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED << manifest, acked >>

Appoint(c) ==
  /\ term < MaxTerm
  /\ leader # c
  /\ term' = term + 1
  /\ leader' = c
  /\ craneTerm' = [craneTerm EXCEPT ![c] = term + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED << manifest, acked >>

ApplyMove(c, m) ==
  /\ leader = c
  /\ craneTerm[c] = term
  /\ m \notin acked
  /\ acked' = acked \cup {m}
  /\ manifest' = manifest \cup {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED << term, leader, craneTerm >>

StaleWriteRejected(c, m) ==
  /\ craneTerm[c] < term
  /\ m \in Moves
  /\ UNCHANGED vars

StepDown ==
  /\ leader # NoLeader
  /\ leader' = NoLeader
  /\ UNCHANGED << term, craneTerm, manifest, acked >>

  \/ \E c \in Cranes : StandForElection(c) \/ Appoint(c) \/ StepDown
  \/ \E c \in Cranes, m \in Moves : ApplyMove(c, m) \/ StaleWriteRejected(c, m)

  /\ acked \subseteq manifest
  /\ manifest \subseteq acked
  /\ \A c \in Cranes : craneTerm[c] <= term
  /\ (leader # NoLeader => craneTerm[leader] = term)
  /\ (manifest # {} => term > 0)
====
nl:
A container crane yard keeps a shared manifest of which moves have been carried out. Only
the elected lead crane may write to the manifest. Leadership is held for a term: any crane
can stand for election with a term number higher than the current one, and doing so
immediately displaces the previous leader, whose later writes are rejected because its
term is stale. That is the yard's failover story when a crane's radio dies mid-shift.

A move is first acknowledged to the ship's agent and then applied to the manifest by the
lead crane. An acknowledged move that never reached the manifest would be a lost update,
which is exactly what the yard cannot tolerate, so the lead crane applies a move to the
manifest at the same instant it acknowledges it.

The yard superintendent has an override: he can appoint a crane as leader directly,
bumping the term himself, which is how a stuck election gets resolved. An appointed leader
is bound by exactly the same term rules as an elected one.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every acknowledged move is present in the manifest, only a crane whose
recorded term equals the current term is leader, no crane's term ever exceeds the current
term, and the manifest never contains a move that was never acknowledged.

  /\ benched' = benched \cup {u}
  /\ UNCHANGED << queue, shelf, turnedAway, placedBy >>

Next ==
  \/ \E st \in Stations, u \in Units, d \in Shelves : FileJob(st, u, d)
  \/ \E u \in Units : TurnAway(u) \/ NewArrival(u)
  \/ \E s \in Shelves : Issue(s)
  \/ PlaceUnit

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

ColdRoomOK ==
  /\ \A s1, s2 \in Shelves :
       (shelf[s1] # Empty /\ shelf[s1] = shelf[s2]) => s1 = s2
  /\ \A i, j \in 1..Len(queue) : queue[i].dest = queue[j].dest => i = j
  /\ \A i \in 1..Len(queue) : shelf[queue[i].dest] = Empty
  /\ Len(queue) <= Depth
  /\ \A i \in 1..Len(queue) : queue[i].unit \notin benched

nl:
A blood bank has two intake stations, the donor floor and the courier dock, working from
one shared pool of arriving units. Both stations file shelf-placement jobs into a single
bounded work queue in front of the cold room. The queue has a fixed depth and applies
backpressure: when it is full a station's filing is turned away and the station holds the
unit on the bench instead of blocking the line.

Units leave the cold room when they are issued to a ward, and a donation bearing a given
unit identifier can arrive again later once no copy of it is on the bench, in the queue,
or on a shelf.

A cold-room technician takes jobs from the head of the queue and places the unit on a
named shelf. Each shelf takes one unit and one only. A job is filed for a shelf only if
that shelf is free and no queued job is already headed for it, so two units are never
routed to the same shelf even though the two stations never talk to each other.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No shelf ever holds two units and no unit is ever on two shelves, no two
queued jobs target the same shelf, no queued job targets a shelf that is already occupied,
and the queue never exceeds its fixed depth.

  /\ (charges = Load => sealed = {})

  Cars = {carA, carB, carC}

INVARIANT SealOK
nl:
A car wash runs cars down a conveyor through a bounded staging queue. Cars enter the
staging queue at the entrance gate; when the queue is at its depth the gate refuses the
next car and it waits in the lot, which is the tunnel's backpressure.

At the far end of the tunnel each car receives the ceramic seal, and the seal is
irreversible: once a car has been sealed the coating is cured and can never be applied
again or stripped. The sealing head can therefore only fire on a car that has come through
the queue and has not been sealed before, and each firing consumes one charge from the
sealant cartridge.

The shift manager has an override switch. With it engaged she can push a car into the
staging queue past the gate's refusal, for instance to finish a car that was already
half-way down the tunnel when the queue backed up. The override lets a car skip the queue
discipline; it never lets a car be sealed twice and it never conjures sealant charges.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No car is ever sealed twice, every sealed car passed through the tunnel
first, no sealed car is still sitting in the tunnel or the staging queue, a full
cartridge means nothing has been sealed yet, and the staging queue only exceeds its normal depth when the
manager's override is engaged.

---- MODULE W4Od10m3p1t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Computers, Blocks, Trains, NoMaster, Clear
MaxGen == 3

VARIABLES gen, master, seenGen, record, confirmed
vars == << gen, master, seenGen, record, confirmed >>

TypeOK ==
  /\ gen \in 0..MaxGen
  /\ master \in Computers \cup {NoMaster}
  /\ seenGen \in [Computers -> 0..MaxGen]
  /\ record \in [Blocks -> Trains \cup {Clear}]
  /\ confirmed \in [Blocks -> Trains \cup {Clear}]

Init ==
  /\ gen = 0
  /\ master = NoMaster
  /\ seenGen = [c \in Computers |-> 0]
  /\ record = [b \in Blocks |-> Clear]
  /\ confirmed = [b \in Blocks |-> Clear]

TakeOver(c) ==
  /\ gen < MaxGen
  /\ master # c
  /\ gen' = gen + 1
  /\ master' = c
  /\ seenGen' = [seenGen EXCEPT ![c] = gen + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED << record, confirmed >>

CatchUp(c) ==
  /\ seenGen[c] < gen
  /\ c # master
  /\ seenGen' = [seenGen EXCEPT ![c] = gen]
  /\ UNCHANGED << gen, master, record, confirmed >>

ConfirmOccupancy(c, b, t) ==
  /\ master = c
  /\ seenGen[c] = gen
  /\ record[b] = Clear
  /\ \A d \in Blocks : record[d] # t
  /\ record' = [record EXCEPT ![b] = t]
  /\ confirmed' = [confirmed EXCEPT ![b] = t]
  /\ UNCHANGED << gen, master, seenGen >>

ClearBlock(c, b) ==
  /\ master = c
  /\ seenGen[c] = gen
  /\ record[b] # Clear
  /\ record' = [record EXCEPT ![b] = Clear]
  /\ confirmed' = [confirmed EXCEPT ![b] = Clear]
  /\ UNCHANGED << gen, master, seenGen >>

StaleWriteIgnored(c, b) ==
  /\ seenGen[c] < gen
  /\ b \in Blocks
  /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in Computers : TakeOver(c) \/ CatchUp(c)
  \/ \E c \in Computers, b \in Blocks : ClearBlock(c, b) \/ StaleWriteIgnored(c, b)
  \/ \E c \in Computers, b \in Blocks, t \in Trains : ConfirmOccupancy(c, b, t)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

SignallingOK ==
  /\ \A b \in Blocks : record[b] = confirmed[b]
  /\ \A c \in Computers : seenGen[c] <= gen
  /\ (master # NoMaster => seenGen[master] = gen)
  /\ \A b1, b2 \in Blocks :
       (record[b1] # Clear /\ record[b1] = record[b2]) => b1 = b2
====
nl:
A subway line divides its track into signalling blocks. A shared occupancy record says
which train is in which block, and only the interlocking computer currently acting as
master may write it. Mastership is held under a numbered generation: a standby computer
takes over by claiming a strictly higher generation, at which point the old master's
writes are ignored because it is writing under an old generation.

One of the standby computers is slow, not failed: it still answers, but its view of the
generation can lag arbitrarily far behind. A slow computer must therefore never be trusted
to write, and when it finally catches up it adopts the current generation rather than
overwriting anything with its stale picture.

The line cannot tolerate a lost update: once the master has confirmed a block occupancy to
the dispatcher, that confirmation must be reflected in the occupancy record. The master
therefore writes the record and confirms in the same step.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every occupancy confirmed to the dispatcher appears in the occupancy
record and nothing appears in the record that was not confirmed, no computer's generation
exceeds the current generation, only a computer running the current generation is master,
and a block never records two different trains.

---- MODULE W4Od12m8p1t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Terminals, Groups, Free
MaxCount == 2

VARIABLES coarse, fine, ledger, scratch, crashed
vars == << coarse, fine, ledger, scratch, crashed >>

NoScratch == [ line |-> Free, val |-> 0 ]

TypeOK ==
  /\ coarse \in Terminals \cup {Free}
  /\ fine \in [Groups -> Terminals \cup {Free}]
  /\ ledger \in [Groups -> 0..MaxCount]
  /\ scratch \in [Terminals -> [line : Groups \cup {Free}, val : 0..MaxCount]]
  /\ crashed \in [Terminals -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
  /\ coarse = Free
  /\ fine = [g \in Groups |-> Free]
  /\ ledger = [g \in Groups |-> 0]
  /\ scratch = [t \in Terminals |-> NoScratch]
  /\ crashed = [t \in Terminals |-> FALSE]

GrabCoarse(t) ==
  /\ ~crashed[t]
  /\ coarse = Free
  /\ scratch[t] = NoScratch
  /\ coarse' = t
  /\ UNCHANGED << fine, ledger, scratch, crashed >>

GrabFine(t, g) ==
  /\ ~crashed[t]
  /\ coarse = t
  /\ fine[g] = Free
  /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![g] = t]
  /\ scratch' = [scratch EXCEPT ![t] = [line |-> g, val |-> ledger[g]]]
  /\ coarse' = Free
  /\ UNCHANGED << ledger, crashed >>

WriteBack(t) ==
  /\ ~crashed[t]
  /\ scratch[t].line \in Groups
  /\ fine[scratch[t].line] = t
  /\ ledger[scratch[t].line] = scratch[t].val
  /\ scratch[t].val < MaxCount
  /\ ledger' = [ledger EXCEPT ![scratch[t].line] = scratch[t].val + 1]
  /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![scratch[t].line] = Free]
  /\ scratch' = [scratch EXCEPT ![t] = NoScratch]
  /\ UNCHANGED << coarse, crashed >>

CrashSilently(t) ==
  /\ ~crashed[t]
  /\ crashed' = [crashed EXCEPT ![t] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED << coarse, fine, ledger, scratch >>

Janitor(t) ==
  /\ crashed[t]
  /\ coarse' = IF coarse = t THEN Free ELSE coarse
  /\ fine' = [g \in Groups |-> IF fine[g] = t THEN Free ELSE fine[g]]
  /\ scratch' = [scratch EXCEPT ![t] = NoScratch]
  /\ crashed' = [crashed EXCEPT ![t] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED ledger

Next ==
  \/ \E t \in Terminals : GrabCoarse(t) \/ WriteBack(t) \/ CrashSilently(t) \/ Janitor(t)
  \/ \E t \in Terminals, g \in Groups : GrabFine(t, g)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

LedgerLocksOK ==
  /\ \A g \in Groups : \A t \in Terminals : fine[g] = t => coarse # t
  /\ \A g \in Groups : \A t \in Terminals :
       fine[g] = t => scratch[t].line \in {g, Free}
  /\ \A t \in Terminals :
       scratch[t].line \in Groups => fine[scratch[t].line] = t
  /\ \A t \in Terminals :
       scratch[t].line \in Groups => scratch[t].val <= ledger[scratch[t].line]
====
nl:
A blood bank keeps a ledger of unit counts per blood group. Updating the ledger takes two
locks in a fixed order: first the coarse ledger lock for the whole book, then the fine
lock for the specific group's line. Taking them in that order is what keeps the branch
terminals from deadlocking against each other.

An update is a read-modify-write: the terminal reads the line's current count into its
own scratch while holding the fine lock, computes a new count, and writes it back before
releasing. No update may be lost -- a write is only accepted if the line still reads what
the terminal read, which the fine lock guarantees while it is held.

A terminal can crash silently at any point. If it crashes holding locks the locks are
recovered by the janitor task, and any half-done update is discarded rather than written,
because a partial read-modify-write is exactly how a count gets clobbered.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The coarse lock and each fine lock are held by at most one terminal, a
terminal that holds a fine lock has already handed the coarse lock back and its pending
scratch is either for that same line or empty, and a terminal's pending read value never
exceeds the count currently on the line it read.

---- MODULE W4Od7m6p2t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Cranes, Stacks, Nobody
Horizon == 2
Term == 2
BoxCount == 4

VARIABLES clock, lessee, expiry, onStack, spreader, loaded
vars == << clock, lessee, expiry, onStack, spreader, loaded >>

RECURSIVE PileSum(_)
PileSum(S) ==
  IF S = {} THEN 0
  ELSE LET s == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN onStack[s] + PileSum(S \ {s})

RECURSIVE Rides(_)
Rides(S) ==
  IF S = {} THEN 0
  ELSE LET c == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE
       IN (IF spreader[c] THEN 1 ELSE 0) + Rides(S \ {c})

TypeOK ==
  /\ clock \in 0..Horizon
  /\ lessee \in [Stacks -> Cranes \cup {Nobody}]
  /\ expiry \in [Stacks -> 0..(Horizon + Term)]
  /\ onStack \in [Stacks -> 0..BoxCount]
  /\ spreader \in [Cranes -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ loaded \in 0..BoxCount

Init ==
  /\ clock = 0
  /\ lessee = [s \in Stacks |-> Nobody]
  /\ expiry = [s \in Stacks |-> 0]
  /\ onStack = [s \in Stacks |-> 2]
  /\ spreader = [c \in Cranes |-> FALSE]
  /\ loaded = 0

Lease(c, s) ==
  /\ lessee[s] = Nobody
  /\ lessee' = [lessee EXCEPT ![s] = c]
  /\ expiry' = [expiry EXCEPT ![s] = clock + Term]
  /\ UNCHANGED << clock, onStack, spreader, loaded >>

Release(s) ==
  /\ lessee[s] # Nobody
  /\ lessee' = [lessee EXCEPT ![s] = Nobody]
  /\ expiry' = [expiry EXCEPT ![s] = 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED << clock, onStack, spreader, loaded >>

ExpireLease(s) ==
  /\ lessee[s] # Nobody
  /\ expiry[s] <= clock
  /\ lessee' = [lessee EXCEPT ![s] = Nobody]
  /\ expiry' = [expiry EXCEPT ![s] = 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED << clock, onStack, spreader, loaded >>

Lift(c, s) ==
  /\ lessee[s] = c
  /\ expiry[s] > clock
  /\ ~spreader[c]
  /\ onStack[s] > 0
  /\ onStack' = [onStack EXCEPT ![s] = onStack[s] - 1]
  /\ spreader' = [spreader EXCEPT ![c] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED << clock, lessee, expiry, loaded >>

SetDown(c, s) ==
  /\ lessee[s] = c
  /\ expiry[s] > clock
  /\ spreader[c]
  /\ onStack' = [onStack EXCEPT ![s] = onStack[s] + 1]
  /\ spreader' = [spreader EXCEPT ![c] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED << clock, lessee, expiry, loaded >>

LoadShip(c) ==
  /\ spreader[c]
  /\ spreader' = [spreader EXCEPT ![c] = FALSE]
  /\ loaded' = loaded + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED << clock, lessee, expiry, onStack >>

TickClock ==
  /\ clock < Horizon
  /\ clock' = clock + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED << lessee, expiry, onStack, spreader, loaded >>

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in Cranes, s \in Stacks : Lease(c, s) \/ Lift(c, s) \/ SetDown(c, s)
  \/ \E s \in Stacks : Release(s) \/ ExpireLease(s)
  \/ \E c \in Cranes : LoadShip(c)
  \/ TickClock

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

YardOK ==
  /\ PileSum(Stacks) + Rides(Cranes) + loaded = BoxCount
  /\ Rides(Cranes) <= Cardinality(Cranes)
  /\ \A s \in Stacks : lessee[s] = Nobody => expiry[s] = 0
  /\ \A s \in Stacks : lessee[s] # Nobody => expiry[s] > 0
====
nl:
In a crane yard the right to work a stack is handed out as a lease with an expiry read off
the yard clock. A crane holding a live lease on a stack may lift a box off that stack onto
its spreader and may set a box down onto it. Leases are requested and released over the
yard radio, which reorders freely: a release message may be processed after a later
request, so the yard only ever trusts the expiry, never the message order. When the clock
passes a lease's expiry the lease is dead and the stack is free again, even if the crane
that held it has not said anything.

Boxes are neither created nor destroyed. Every box is on the stack, riding a crane's
spreader, or already loaded on the ship. A crane carries at most one box, and a box that
is on a spreader when its crane's lease dies stays on the spreader until it is put down
under a fresh lease.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The boxes on the stack, the boxes riding cranes, and the boxes loaded on
the ship always sum to the yard's fixed box count, no crane rides more than one box, a
stack lease is held by at most one crane, and a stack with no lease has no recorded expiry.

---- MODULE W4Od12m0p5t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Units, Clerks
Opening == 3
MaxFloor == 2

VARIABLES issued, revision, cached, floor
vars == << issued, revision, cached, floor >>

Stock == Opening - Cardinality(issued)

TypeOK ==
  /\ issued \subseteq Units
  /\ revision \in [Units -> 0..1]
  /\ cached \in [Clerks -> [Units -> 0..1]]
  /\ floor \in 0..MaxFloor

Init ==
  /\ issued = {}
  /\ revision = [u \in Units |-> 0]
  /\ cached = [c \in Clerks |-> [u \in Units |-> 0]]
  /\ floor = 0

ReadLine(c, u) ==
  /\ cached' = [cached EXCEPT ![c][u] = revision[u]]
  /\ UNCHANGED << issued, revision, floor >>

MarkIssued(c, u) ==
  /\ cached[c][u] = revision[u]
  /\ u \notin issued
  /\ Stock > floor
  /\ issued' = issued \cup {u}
  /\ revision' = [revision EXCEPT ![u] = 1]
  /\ cached' = [cached EXCEPT ![c][u] = 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED floor

RejectMark(c, u) ==
  /\ cached[c][u] # revision[u]
  /\ cached' = [cached EXCEPT ![c][u] = revision[u]]
  /\ UNCHANGED << issued, revision, floor >>

BlockedByFloor(c, u) ==
  /\ Stock <= floor
  /\ u \notin issued
  /\ c \in Clerks
  /\ UNCHANGED vars

SetFloor(f) ==
  /\ f \in 0..MaxFloor
  /\ f # floor
  /\ floor' = f
  /\ UNCHANGED << issued, revision, cached >>

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in Clerks, u \in Units :
       ReadLine(c, u) \/ MarkIssued(c, u) \/ RejectMark(c, u) \/ BlockedByFloor(c, u)
  \/ \E f \in 0..MaxFloor : SetFloor(f)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

IssueOK ==
  /\ \A u \in Units : (u \in issued) = (revision[u] = 1)
  /\ \A c \in Clerks, u \in Units : cached[c][u] <= revision[u]
  /\ Stock >= 0
  /\ Cardinality(issued) <= Opening
  /\ \A u \in Units : u \notin issued => revision[u] = 0
====
nl:
A blood bank issues units to wards through an optimistically-locked issue register. Each
unit's register line carries a revision number. A ward clerk reads a unit's line, then
tries to mark the unit issued; the mark only takes if the revision is still the one the
clerk read, otherwise the attempt is rejected and the clerk must re-read and retry. Every
successful mark bumps the revision.

Issuing a unit is irreversible: once a unit has been transfused it can never be
un-transfused, re-issued, or returned to stock, so the register must ensure a unit is
marked issued at most once no matter how many clerks race for it.

The cold room's reserve requirement changes during the day: the bank must always keep at
least a floor of units in stock, and the duty haematologist can raise or lower that floor
at runtime. A clerk may not issue a unit that would take stock below the floor currently
in force, though lowering or raising the floor never changes what has already been issued.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A unit is never marked issued twice, an issued unit's revision is above
zero while an untouched unit's revision is zero, no clerk's cached revision is ever ahead
of the register's, and the stock remaining, which is the opening stock less the units
issued, never goes negative.

---- MODULE W4Od2m5p3t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Robots, Bays, NoOne

Majority == 2

VARIABLES claimant, ballots, awarded, crashed, docked
vars == << claimant, ballots, awarded, crashed, docked >>

TypeOK ==
  /\ claimant \in [Bays -> Robots \cup {NoOne}]
  /\ ballots \in [Bays -> SUBSET Robots]
  /\ awarded \in [Bays -> Robots \cup {NoOne}]
  /\ crashed \in [Robots -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ docked \subseteq Robots

Init ==
  /\ claimant = [b \in Bays |-> NoOne]
  /\ ballots = [b \in Bays |-> {}]
  /\ awarded = [b \in Bays |-> NoOne]
  /\ crashed = [r \in Robots |-> FALSE]
  /\ docked = {}

OpenClaim(r, b) ==
  /\ ~crashed[r]
  /\ claimant[b] = NoOne
  /\ awarded[b] = NoOne
  /\ r \notin docked
  /\ \A c \in Bays : claimant[c] # r
  /\ claimant' = [claimant EXCEPT ![b] = r]
  /\ ballots' = [ballots EXCEPT ![b] = {r}]
  /\ UNCHANGED << awarded, crashed, docked >>

Vote(v, b) ==
  /\ ~crashed[v]
  /\ claimant[b] # NoOne
  /\ v \notin ballots[b]
  /\ ballots' = [ballots EXCEPT ![b] = ballots[b] \cup {v}]
  /\ UNCHANGED << claimant, awarded, crashed, docked >>

Award(b) ==
  /\ claimant[b] # NoOne
  /\ awarded[b] = NoOne
  /\ Cardinality(ballots[b]) >= Majority
  /\ awarded' = [awarded EXCEPT ![b] = claimant[b]]
  /\ docked' = docked \cup {claimant[b]}
  /\ claimant' = [claimant EXCEPT ![b] = NoOne]
  /\ ballots' = [ballots EXCEPT ![b] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED crashed

CrashSilently(r) ==
  /\ ~crashed[r]
  /\ crashed' = [crashed EXCEPT ![r] = TRUE]
  /\ claimant' = [b \in Bays |-> IF claimant[b] = r THEN NoOne ELSE claimant[b]]
  /\ ballots' = [b \in Bays |-> IF claimant[b] = r THEN {} ELSE ballots[b] \ {r}]
  /\ UNCHANGED << awarded, docked >>

Watchdog(b) ==
  /\ awarded[b] # NoOne
  /\ crashed[awarded[b]]
  /\ docked' = docked \ {awarded[b]}
  /\ awarded' = [awarded EXCEPT ![b] = NoOne]
  /\ UNCHANGED << claimant, ballots, crashed >>

Undock(b) ==
  /\ awarded[b] # NoOne
  /\ ~crashed[awarded[b]]
  /\ docked' = docked \ {awarded[b]}
  /\ awarded' = [awarded EXCEPT ![b] = NoOne]
  /\ UNCHANGED << claimant, ballots, crashed >>

Reboot(r) ==
  /\ crashed[r]
  /\ \A b \in Bays : awarded[b] # r
  /\ crashed' = [crashed EXCEPT ![r] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED << claimant, ballots, awarded, docked >>

Next ==
  \/ \E r \in Robots, b \in Bays : OpenClaim(r, b) \/ Vote(r, b)
  \/ \E b \in Bays : Award(b) \/ Watchdog(b) \/ Undock(b)
  \/ \E r \in Robots : CrashSilently(r) \/ Reboot(r)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

BayAwardOK ==
  /\ \A b1, b2 \in Bays :
       (awarded[b1] # NoOne /\ awarded[b1] = awarded[b2]) => b1 = b2
  /\ \A b \in Bays : awarded[b] # NoOne => awarded[b] \in docked
  /\ \A b \in Bays : claimant[b] = NoOne => ballots[b] = {}
  /\ \A b \in Bays : claimant[b] # NoOne => ~crashed[claimant[b]]
  /\ \A r \in docked : \E b \in Bays : awarded[b] = r
====
nl:
A warehouse robot fleet allocates charging bays by quorum vote. A robot that wants a bay
puts the bay up for a vote; every other robot that is still alive votes for at most one
candidate per bay, and the bay is awarded only when a strict majority of the fleet has
voted for the same claimant. An awarded bay belongs to that robot until it undocks.

A robot can crash silently. A crashed robot casts no votes, cannot be awarded a bay, and has any
open claim of its own torn down at once; if it crashes while holding a bay the fleet's
watchdog frees the bay, and once it holds nothing it can be rebooted back into service. Because
crashed robots simply stop answering, a claim can sit unresolved forever, which is
tolerable -- what is not tolerable is a bay awarded to two robots.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No robot is awarded two bays, an awarded robot is exactly a docked robot
and every docked robot has a bay, a bay with no open claim carries no ballots, and the
claimant of an open claim is never a crashed robot.

---- MODULE W4Od17m1p0t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Nodes, Instances, Bags, Idle

Succ(n) == CHOOSE m \in Nodes : m # n

VARIABLES token, attached, arm, working, sorted
vars == << token, attached, arm, working, sorted >>

TypeOK ==
  /\ token \in Nodes
  /\ attached \in [Instances -> Nodes]
  /\ arm \in Instances \cup {Idle}
  /\ working \in [Instances -> Bags \cup {Idle}]
  /\ sorted \subseteq Bags

Init ==
  /\ token \in Nodes
  /\ attached \in [Instances -> Nodes]
  /\ arm = Idle
  /\ working = [i \in Instances |-> Idle]
  /\ sorted = {}

PickBag(i, b) ==
  /\ working[i] = Idle
  /\ b \notin sorted
  /\ \A j \in Instances : working[j] # b
  /\ working' = [working EXCEPT ![i] = b]
  /\ UNCHANGED << token, attached, arm, sorted >>

SeizeArm(i) ==
  /\ arm = Idle
  /\ working[i] # Idle
  /\ attached[i] = token
  /\ arm' = i
  /\ UNCHANGED << token, attached, working, sorted >>

Divert(i) ==
  /\ arm = i
  /\ working[i] # Idle
  /\ sorted' = sorted \cup {working[i]}
  /\ working' = [working EXCEPT ![i] = Idle]
  /\ arm' = Idle
  /\ UNCHANGED << token, attached >>

PassToken ==
  /\ arm = Idle
  /\ token' = Succ(token)
  /\ UNCHANGED << attached, arm, working, sorted >>

Reattach(i, n) ==
  /\ working[i] = Idle
  /\ arm # i
  /\ attached[i] # n
  /\ attached' = [attached EXCEPT ![i] = n]
  /\ UNCHANGED << token, arm, working, sorted >>

Rescan(b) ==
  /\ b \in sorted
  /\ \A j \in Instances : working[j] # b
  /\ sorted' = sorted \ {b}
  /\ UNCHANGED << token, attached, arm, working >>

Next ==
  \/ \E i \in Instances, b \in Bags : PickBag(i, b)
  \/ \E i \in Instances : SeizeArm(i) \/ Divert(i)
  \/ \E i \in Instances, n \in Nodes : Reattach(i, n)
  \/ \E b \in Bags : Rescan(b)
  \/ PassToken

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

DiverterOK ==
  /\ (arm # Idle => attached[arm] = token)
  /\ (arm # Idle => working[arm] # Idle)
  /\ \A i, j \in Instances :
       (working[i] # Idle /\ working[i] = working[j]) => i = j
  /\ \A i \in Instances : working[i] # Idle => working[i] \notin sorted
====
nl:
An airport baggage router has two independent sorter instances, north and south, that
share one pool of bags. Both need the diverter arm, and only one may drive it at a time.
The right to drive the arm circulates as a token around a ring of control nodes. A node
that wants to drive the arm waits until the token reaches it, drives, then passes the
token to its ring successor.

Because the two sorter instances draw bags from the same pool, a bag can be picked up by
either instance, and once an instance is working a bag no other instance may take it. An
instance can only send a bag through the diverter while the node it is attached to holds
the token and the arm is not already in use.

SAFETY PROPERTY: An instance driving the diverter arm always has a bag in hand and is
attached to the node that currently holds the token, no bag is ever being worked by both
sorter instances at once, and a bag in hand is never already recorded as sorted.

---- MODULE W4Od2m8p4t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Robots, Shelves, Nobody
Limit == 2

VARIABLES aisleLock, shelfLock, inside, picked, lingering
vars == << aisleLock, shelfLock, inside, picked, lingering >>

Holder(s) == shelfLock[s]

TypeOK ==
  /\ aisleLock \in Robots \cup {Nobody}
  /\ shelfLock \in [Shelves -> Robots \cup {Nobody}]
  /\ inside \subseteq Robots
  /\ picked \subseteq Shelves
  /\ lingering \subseteq Robots

Init ==
  /\ aisleLock = Nobody
  /\ shelfLock = [s \in Shelves |-> Nobody]
  /\ inside = {}
  /\ picked = {}
  /\ lingering = {}

EnterAisle(r) ==
  /\ aisleLock = Nobody
  /\ r \notin inside
  /\ Cardinality(inside) < Limit
  /\ aisleLock' = r
  /\ inside' = inside \cup {r}
  /\ UNCHANGED << shelfLock, picked, lingering >>

TakeShelf(r, s) ==
  /\ aisleLock = r
  /\ shelfLock[s] = Nobody
  /\ \A t \in Shelves : shelfLock[t] # r
  /\ shelfLock' = [shelfLock EXCEPT ![s] = r]
  /\ aisleLock' = Nobody
  /\ UNCHANGED << inside, picked, lingering >>

PickShelf(r, s) ==
  /\ shelfLock[s] = r
  /\ s \notin picked
  /\ picked' = picked \cup {s}
  /\ UNCHANGED << aisleLock, shelfLock, inside, lingering >>

LeaveShelf(r, s) ==
  /\ shelfLock[s] = r
  /\ s \in picked
  /\ r \notin lingering
  /\ shelfLock' = [shelfLock EXCEPT ![s] = Nobody]
  /\ inside' = inside \ {r}
  /\ lingering' = lingering \ {r}
  /\ UNCHANGED << aisleLock, picked >>

Restock(s) ==
  /\ s \in picked
  /\ shelfLock[s] = Nobody
  /\ picked' = picked \ {s}
  /\ UNCHANGED << aisleLock, shelfLock, inside, lingering >>

GiveUpAisle(r) ==
  /\ aisleLock = r
  /\ r \notin lingering
  /\ \A s \in Shelves : shelfLock[s] # r
  /\ aisleLock' = Nobody
  /\ inside' = inside \ {r}
  /\ UNCHANGED << shelfLock, picked, lingering >>

Linger(r) ==
  /\ r \in inside
  /\ r \notin lingering
  /\ lingering' = lingering \cup {r}
  /\ UNCHANGED << aisleLock, shelfLock, inside, picked >>

Resume(r) ==
  /\ r \in lingering
  /\ lingering' = lingering \ {r}
  /\ UNCHANGED << aisleLock, shelfLock, inside, picked >>

Next ==
  \/ \E r \in Robots : EnterAisle(r) \/ GiveUpAisle(r) \/ Linger(r) \/ Resume(r)
  \/ \E r \in Robots, s \in Shelves : TakeShelf(r, s) \/ PickShelf(r, s) \/ LeaveShelf(r, s)
  \/ \E s \in Shelves : Restock(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

AisleOK ==
  /\ Cardinality(inside) <= Limit
  /\ \A s \in Shelves : shelfLock[s] # Nobody => shelfLock[s] \in inside
  /\ \A s \in Shelves : shelfLock[s] # Nobody => aisleLock # shelfLock[s]
  /\ \A s, t \in Shelves :
       (shelfLock[s] # Nobody /\ shelfLock[s] = shelfLock[t]) => s = t
  /\ (aisleLock # Nobody => aisleLock \in inside)
  /\ lingering \subseteq inside
====
nl:
Warehouse picking robots enter aisles under a two-level lock scheme. To work a shelf a
robot must first take the aisle's coarse lock, and only while holding it may it take the
fine lock on the individual shelf; it then releases the aisle lock and works the shelf.
Taking the coarse lock before the fine one is the rule that keeps two robots from grabbing
each other's shelves in opposite order.

The aisle has a hard occupancy limit set by the fire code: only so many robots may be
inside an aisle at once, counting robots that are working a shelf and robots that are
still holding the aisle lock on their way in. A robot that would push the aisle over its
limit simply does not enter.

Robots can be slow rather than broken. A robot inside the aisle may go into a lingering
stall and stay there arbitrarily long, still holding whatever locks it has; while it is
lingering it cannot leave the aisle or hand back the aisle lock. It resumes eventually.
Slowness must never be allowed to break the occupancy limit. Only robots inside the aisle
can be lingering.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of robots inside the aisle never exceeds the fire-code limit,
each shelf's fine lock is held by at most one robot and only by a robot that is inside the
aisle, a robot holding a fine lock does not also hold the aisle's coarse lock, no robot holds two shelves at
once, and every lingering robot is one that is inside the aisle.

EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Movers, Tiers, Nobody
Population == 4

VARIABLES lobby, queued, playing, regionLock, tierLock, override
vars == << lobby, queued, playing, regionLock, tierLock, override >>

TypeOK ==
  /\ lobby \in 0..Population
  /\ queued \in 0..Population
  /\ playing \in 0..Population
  /\ regionLock \in Movers \cup {Nobody}
  /\ tierLock \in [Tiers -> Movers \cup {Nobody}]
  /\ override \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
  /\ lobby = Population
  /\ queued = 0
  /\ playing = 0
  /\ regionLock = Nobody
  /\ tierLock = [t \in Tiers |-> Nobody]
  /\ override = FALSE

TakeRegion(m) ==
  /\ regionLock = Nobody
  /\ \A t \in Tiers : tierLock[t] # m
  /\ regionLock' = m
  /\ UNCHANGED << lobby, queued, playing, tierLock, override >>

TakeTier(m, t) ==
  /\ regionLock = m
  /\ tierLock[t] = Nobody
  /\ tierLock' = [tierLock EXCEPT ![t] = m]
  /\ regionLock' = Nobody
  /\ UNCHANGED << lobby, queued, playing, override >>

OverrideTier(m, t) ==
  /\ override
  /\ regionLock # m
  /\ tierLock[t] = Nobody
  /\ \A u \in Tiers : tierLock[u] # m
  /\ tierLock' = [tierLock EXCEPT ![t] = m]
  /\ UNCHANGED << lobby, queued, playing, regionLock, override >>

Enqueue(m, t) ==
  /\ tierLock[t] = m
  /\ lobby > 0
  /\ lobby' = lobby - 1
  /\ queued' = queued + 1
  /\ tierLock' = [tierLock EXCEPT ![t] = Nobody]
  /\ UNCHANGED << playing, regionLock, override >>

StartMatch(m, t) ==
  /\ tierLock[t] = m
  /\ queued > 0
  /\ queued' = queued - 1
  /\ playing' = playing + 1
  /\ tierLock' = [tierLock EXCEPT ![t] = Nobody]
  /\ UNCHANGED << lobby, regionLock, override >>

EndMatch(m, t) ==
  /\ tierLock[t] = m
  /\ playing > 0
  /\ playing' = playing - 1
  /\ lobby' = lobby + 1
  /\ tierLock' = [tierLock EXCEPT ![t] = Nobody]
  /\ UNCHANGED << queued, regionLock, override >>

ToggleOverride ==
  /\ override' = ~override
  /\ UNCHANGED << lobby, queued, playing, regionLock, tierLock >>

Next ==
  \/ \E m \in Movers : TakeRegion(m)
  \/ \E m \in Movers, t \in Tiers :
       TakeTier(m, t) \/ OverrideTier(m, t) \/ Enqueue(m, t)
         \/ StartMatch(m, t) \/ EndMatch(m, t)
  \/ ToggleOverride

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

ShardOK ==
  /\ lobby + queued + playing = Population
  /\ lobby >= 0 /\ queued >= 0 /\ playing >= 0
  /\ \A t \in Tiers : tierLock[t] # Nobody => regionLock # tierLock[t]
  /\ \A t, u \in Tiers :
       (tierLock[t] # Nobody /\ tierLock[t] = tierLock[u]) => t = u
====
nl:
A multiplayer matchmaker moves players between three places: the regional lobby, the
matchmaking queue, and live matches. Moving a player takes two locks in order: the coarse
region lock covering the whole shard, then the fine lock on the specific queue tier the
player is being moved through. Only after both are held does the move happen, and the
region lock is handed back as soon as the tier lock is taken.

Players are never created or lost by the matchmaker. Every player on the shard is in the
lobby, in the queue, or in a match; a move only ever shifts a player from one of those
places to another.

A live operator holds an admin override. With it engaged the operator can move a player
without taking the region lock -- to pull a griefer out of a match, for instance -- but the
tier lock is still respected, and an override move shifts players exactly like an ordinary
one: one player leaves one place and arrives in another.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The players in the lobby, in the queue, and in matches always sum to the
shard's fixed population, the region lock and each tier lock are held by at most one mover,
a mover holding a tier lock is not also holding the region lock, and no count ever goes
negative.

---- MODULE W4Od5m9p3t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Slots, Parties, Workers, Vacant
MaxEpoch == 2

VARIABLES epoch, cache, seat, seatedAt, refusals
vars == << epoch, cache, seat, seatedAt, refusals >>

TypeOK ==
  /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
  /\ cache \in [Workers -> 0..MaxEpoch]
  /\ seat \in [Slots -> Parties \cup {Vacant}]
  /\ seatedAt \in [Slots -> 0..MaxEpoch]
  /\ refusals \in 0..2

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ cache = [w \in Workers |-> 0]
  /\ seat = [s \in Slots |-> Vacant]
  /\ seatedAt = [s \in Slots |-> 0]
  /\ refusals = 0

Publish ==
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED << cache, seat, seatedAt, refusals >>

PullConfig(w) ==
  /\ cache[w] < epoch
  /\ cache' = [cache EXCEPT ![w] = epoch]
  /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, seat, seatedAt, refusals >>

SeatParty(w, s, p) ==
  /\ cache[w] = epoch
  /\ seat[s] = Vacant
  /\ \A t \in Slots : seat[t] # p
  /\ seat' = [seat EXCEPT ![s] = p]
  /\ seatedAt' = [seatedAt EXCEPT ![s] = epoch]
  /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, cache, refusals >>

RefuseStale(w, s) ==
  /\ cache[w] < epoch
  /\ s \in Slots
  /\ refusals < 2
  /\ refusals' = refusals + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, cache, seat, seatedAt >>

EndMatch(s) ==
  /\ seat[s] # Vacant
  /\ seat' = [seat EXCEPT ![s] = Vacant]
  /\ seatedAt' = [seatedAt EXCEPT ![s] = 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, cache, refusals >>

Next ==
  \/ Publish
  \/ \E w \in Workers : PullConfig(w)
  \/ \E w \in Workers, s \in Slots : RefuseStale(w, s)
  \/ \E w \in Workers, s \in Slots, p \in Parties : SeatParty(w, s, p)
  \/ \E s \in Slots : EndMatch(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

SeatingOK ==
  /\ \A s, t \in Slots : (seat[s] # Vacant /\ seat[s] = seat[t]) => s = t
  /\ \A w \in Workers : cache[w] <= epoch
  /\ \A s \in Slots : seat[s] = Vacant => seatedAt[s] = 0
  /\ \A s \in Slots : seat[s] # Vacant => seatedAt[s] <= epoch
====
nl:
A game lobby matchmaker seats players into numbered match slots on a shard. The seating
rules are versioned: whenever the operators change the skill bands they publish a new
configuration epoch. Each matchmaking worker caches the epoch it last pulled, and the
seating service refuses a seat request from a worker whose cached epoch is behind the
published one, because that worker would be seating players against the old bands.

One worker is slow rather than failed. It keeps answering and keeps issuing requests, but
its cached epoch can lag several publications behind, so its requests are simply refused
until it pulls the current configuration. Refusals are counted so operators can see the
lag.

A slot seats one party and one only. A seated slot is released when the match ends, and
only then may another party be seated there.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No slot ever seats two parties and no party ever occupies two slots, no worker's cached epoch is ever ahead of the published epoch, a vacant slot
carries no seating epoch, and a seated slot's recorded epoch never runs ahead of the
published epoch.
